scope.environmentPolicy: Tune anomaly gameplay effects only; do not tune weather or emission occurrence.

parameters.label: Human Enemy HP
parameters.description: Changes how much damage human enemies can take before they die.
parameters.rationale:
How many bullets a human enemy can soak up before going down. Higher = longer, more ammo-hungry firefights; lower = enemies drop fast.

Vanilla: Novice 1×, Stalker 1.2×, Veteran 1×, Master 1.5×. Pair it with Weapon Damage — both set your time-to-kill, so raising one and lowering the other stacks hard.
parameters.interaction: Weapon Damage affects the same time-to-kill from the opposite side. Raising enemy health while lowering your weapon damage compounds the effect.

parameters.label: Enemy Gun Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much damage you take from firearm hits by human enemies.
parameters.rationale:
How much it hurts when a human enemy shoots you. Low values let you tank a burst; high values make every exposed second dangerous.

Vanilla: Novice 0.17×, Stalker 0.85×, Veteran 1.02×, Master 1.35×. Mutant bites and explosions have their own settings.
parameters.interaction: Human Enemy HP controls how long enemies survive; this controls how dangerous their shots are. Repeated-Hit Protection can also affect how sustained incoming fire feels.

parameters.label: Explosion Damage
parameters.description: Changes damage from explosions such as grenades and other explosive effects.
parameters.rationale:
How deadly grenades and other blasts are — both yours and the enemy's. Raise it if you want grenades to feel lethal, lower it to survive the odd F1 at your feet.

Vanilla: Novice 0.25×, Stalker and Veteran 1×, Master 1.2×.
parameters.interaction: Each explosion still has its own base damage. This setting scales the difficulty layer applied on top of those base values.

parameters.label: Grenades
parameters.description: How often a squad of human enemies may throw a grenade. Rate r divides the pause of the CombatSynchronizer group tokens ThrowGrenade, Special.ThrowGrenade (all enemy ranks) on the selected difficulty.

notes: Group token pauses decide how often anyone in the fight may start this action; Easy/Medium/Hard inherit the Default table, Master owns its own (CombatSynchronizerStalker).
The four full rank tables are written together with SPECIAL ABILITY RATE and the other tactics (one writer).

parameters.rationale: How often human enemies throw grenades at you. Vanilla: every 20–35 s per squad; Master halves it (10–17 s). 2× = twice as often; 0.5× = half as often. The card shows the resulting pause (throws a grenade every 20–35 s at 1×).
parameters.logic: 1× keeps the selected difficulty's own pauses. The rate divides the pause of every enemy rank; who may act still depends on the game's tactics.
parameters.interaction: Other tactics, ENEMY ACCURACY and HUMAN AWARENESS are independent. Enemy gun damage is in HUMAN ENEMY COMBAT.

parameters.label: Enemy Accuracy
parameters.description: Scales how tightly human enemies group their shots: divides DispersionRadius of all 77 NPC weapon settings (75 base game, 2 DLC1).

notes: DispersionRadius is the NPC weapon's own bullet spread (e.g. AK74 300); the distance curve and the zombie addend are unchanged.
Not changed by the game's difficulty; 1x is vanilla on every difficulty.

parameters.rationale: How accurately human enemies shoot. Vanilla: 1×. 2× = half the spread, so more bullets find you at range; 0.5× = twice the spread. Damage per hit is ENEMY GUN DAMAGE.
parameters.logic: Accuracy a divides every NPC weapon's DispersionRadius by a. 1× keeps the game's spread.
parameters.interaction: Independent of the tactics; ENEMY GUN DAMAGE sets how much each hit hurts.

parameters.label: Enemy Sight
parameters.description: Scales how far human enemies see: CentralVisionDistance (80 m) and PeripheralVisionDistance (25 m) of the DefaultNPC vision scanner. Maximum 2.5x = 200 m ahead / 62.5 m peripheral.

notes: Human NPCs use the DefaultNPC vision scanner (ObjPrototypes NPCBase); bosses and zombies inherit from it.
Light, distance and angle penalty curves are unchanged.

parameters.rationale: How far human enemies can spot you. Vanilla: 80 m straight ahead, 25 m at the edge of vision. 0.5× = sneak much closer; 1.5× = they notice you from further away. Maximum 2.5× = 200 m ahead, 62.5 m at the sides.
parameters.logic: Both vision distances are multiplied. Darkness, flashlights and night vision still change what they see.
parameters.interaction: SIGHT, HEARING and MEMORY are independent; together they decide how easy stealth is. Mutants use their own senses and are not changed.

parameters.label: Enemy Hearing
parameters.description: Scales how far human enemies hear sounds: every non-zero HearingDistance of the base hearing sensor (shots 46 m, steps 12 m, voice 30 m, reload 7.5 m, explosions 60 m …).

notes: Human NPCs use DefaultNPC, which inherits the base sensor; zombie humans follow where they do not override. Mutants have their own sensor (unchanged).

parameters.rationale: How far human enemies hear you. Vanilla: footsteps 12 m, gunshots 46 m. 0.5× = you can move and shoot closer unnoticed; 2× = every step gives you away.
parameters.logic: Every sound distance is multiplied (zero entries stay zero).
parameters.interaction: SIGHT, HEARING and MEMORY are independent; together they decide how easy stealth is. Mutants use their own senses and are not changed.

parameters.label: Enemy Memory
parameters.description: Scales how long human enemies keep hunting you after losing track: DefaultNPC threat freeze time (30 s) and SearchEnemy freeze (30 s) are multiplied, their per-second threat loss divided.

notes: Threat memory of human NPCs; BossNPC inherits it. Individual threat sources (ConfidenceDropToZeroTimeSeconds) are unchanged.

parameters.rationale: How long human enemies keep searching after they lose you. Vanilla: they hold their alert about 30 s. 2× = they hunt you twice as long; 0.5× = they give up quickly.
parameters.logic: Freeze times are multiplied and the threat loss per second divided, so the whole alert lasts m times as long.
parameters.interaction: SIGHT, HEARING and MEMORY are independent; together they decide how easy stealth is. Mutants use their own senses and are not changed.

parameters.label: Fog Visibility
parameters.description: Changes the Fogy weather VisibilityCoef in AISettings. This is the actual weather coefficient (0.70 vanilla), not a guaranteed NPC sight range. Other weather, hearing, flair and luminance are untouched.

notes: STALKER 2 2.1 GameData/AIGlobals.cfg: AISettings > WeatherSettings > [2] has WeatherSID = Fogy, VisibilityCoef = 0.7, HearingDistanceCoef = 0.7 and FlairCoef = 0.7.
Runtime behavior and affected AI agent classes are unverified: this is a global weather AI coefficient, not proven human-only.
Do not change the separate fog luminance value (0.6f), hearing or flair.

parameters.rationale: How well human enemies see through fog. Vanilla: 70% of their clear-weather sight. Lower = fog hides you better; 100% = fog gives you no cover. Real spotting range also depends on light and cover.
parameters.logic: Writes only AISettings.WeatherSettings[2].VisibilityCoef in GameData/AIGlobals.cfg (Fogy), preserving all other weather, hearing, flair and luminance values.
parameters.interaction: Independent of SIGHT (always-on scanner range). This coefficient may apply to any AI using the global weather setting; needs an in-game 2.1 acceptance test.

parameters.label: Rain Noise
parameters.description: How much light or regular rain masks sounds from AI. Higher noise means less enemy hearing.

notes: Original STALKER 2.1 AIGlobals.cfg WeatherSettings 3/4 has Rainy and LightRainy HearingDistanceCoef = 0.7.
Global AI weather coefficient; effects and AI-class scope still need an in-game test.

parameters.rationale: How much rain covers your noise. Vanilla: 30% — in rain enemies hear you at 70% of the normal range. Higher = sneak closer while it pours; 0% = rain gives you no cover.
parameters.logic: Displayed masking percent = (1 - HearingDistanceCoef) x 100. Presets and writer keep native coefficient and write only WeatherSettings[3] and [4].HearingDistanceCoef.
parameters.interaction: Only active during light or regular rain; independent of general HEARING. UI masking range is 0-90%, 5% steps.

parameters.label: Thunder Noise
parameters.description: How much thunder masks sounds from AI. Higher noise means less enemy hearing.

notes: Original STALKER 2.1 AIGlobals.cfg WeatherSettings 5 has Thundery HearingDistanceCoef = 0.6.
Global AI weather coefficient; effects and AI-class scope still need an in-game test.

parameters.rationale: How much a thunderstorm covers your noise. Vanilla: 40% — enemies hear you at 60% of the normal range. Higher = thunder hides your steps and shots better; 0% = no cover.
parameters.logic: Displayed masking percent = (1 - HearingDistanceCoef) x 100. Presets and writer keep native coefficient and write only WeatherSettings[5].HearingDistanceCoef.
parameters.interaction: Only active during thunder; independent of general HEARING. UI masking range is 0-90%, 5% steps.

parameters.label: Weapon Damage
parameters.description: Changes the base damage dealt by your weapons.
parameters.rationale:
The damage your own guns deal on a normal body hit. Lower values mean more bullets per kill and more ammo burned.

Vanilla: Novice 1.3×, Stalker 1×, Veteran and Master 0.75×. Headshots get an extra boost on top from Headshot Damage.
parameters.interaction: Headshot Damage adds another layer on headshots. Human Enemy HP also changes the final time-to-kill.

parameters.label: Headshot Damage
parameters.description: Scales the damage multiplier applied to your headshots; 1x is normal and 2x doubles the configured headshot damage.
parameters.rationale:
Extra punch for your headshots on top of normal weapon damage. 2× doubles the headshot bonus, rewarding careful aim over spraying.

Vanilla: 1× on every difficulty except Master, which uses 2×.
parameters.logic: 1.0x is the normal multiplier. 2.0x doubles the headshot damage multiplier used by the selected Base Preset; it is not an additive extra-damage percentage.
parameters.interaction: Weapon Damage also affects the underlying hit. The headshot multiplier scales that hit; changing both settings compounds their effect.

parameters.label: Weapon Jam Rate
parameters.description: Changes how often worn weapons jam.
parameters.rationale:
How often worn guns jam on you. Higher values make maintenance and weapon condition matter much more; 0.5× halves jams.

Vanilla: 1× on Novice, Stalker and Veteran; Master 1.5×. A gun in good condition still rarely jams.
parameters.interaction: Weapon condition and each weapon's own jam behavior still matter. Use this to make jams generally more or less common.

parameters.label: Mutant Hit Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much damage mutant attacks deal when they connect.
parameters.rationale:
How hard mutants hit when they reach you — bites, claws and charges. Mutant toughness is set separately in the health cards.

Vanilla: Novice 0.35×, Stalker 1×, Veteran 1.35×, Master 1.5×.
parameters.interaction: Mutant Health controls how much damage they can absorb; this control changes only damage dealt to the player.

parameters.label: Peak Hit Protection
parameters.description: Sets the stronger end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.rationale:
The game quietly softens damage when many hits land at once, so you don't melt in a single burst. This is the strongest that safety net can get.

Higher = more forgiving under heavy fire, lower = bursts hit closer to full damage. Vanilla: Novice 1, Stalker 0.75, Veteran 0.5, Master 0.4.
parameters.logic: Higher values give more protection against rapid hits; lower values make them harsher. The number is protection strength, not a literal damage-reduction percentage.
parameters.interaction: Minimum Hit Protection sets the weakest protection in the same repeated-hit system. Incoming gun damage is independent.

parameters.label: Minimum Hit Protection
parameters.description: Sets the weaker end of the hidden protection the game can apply when several hits land close together.
parameters.rationale:
The weakest end of the same hidden safety net against rapid hits. Raising it keeps some protection even in long, sustained fights.

Vanilla: Novice 1, Stalker 0.33, Veteran 0.15, Master 0.12. Works together with Peak Hit Protection.
parameters.logic: Higher values give more protection at the weak end; lower values make rapid hits harsher. This is not a literal damage-reduction percentage.
parameters.interaction: Peak Hit Protection sets the strongest protection in the same system. Incoming gun damage is independent.

parameters.label: Healed Damage Still Counts
parameters.description: Controls whether damage remains in the repeated-hit protection tracker after you heal it.
parameters.rationale:
Decides whether hits you already healed still count against your burst protection. ON (Veteran, Master) means patching up mid-fight doesn't reset the safety net; OFF (Novice, Stalker) is more forgiving.

Healing itself always restores your HP normally.
parameters.logic: OFF matches Novice and Stalker. ON matches Veteran and Master. Healing always restores HP normally; this toggle only decides whether the healed portion is still remembered by the repeated-hit protection system.
parameters.interaction: Works with Minimum and Peak Hit Protection; healing always restores HP even when past hits remain counted.

parameters.label: Bloodsucker Health

notes: Directly scales the authored MaxHP field in GameData/ObjPrototypes.cfg.
1x is vanilla.
This is not selected through DifficultyPrototypes.cfg; the same generated MaxHP applies regardless of the in-game difficulty.
The Bloodsucker family control applies the same multiplier to Bloodsucker (500 MaxHP) and MistBloodsucker (1000 MaxHP); the radar displays the standard Bloodsucker value only.

Variants with their own MaxHP follow the same multiplier: AshyBloodsucker, PrologueBloodsucker. Collar variants inherit from the base prototype; illusion clones (Bayun clone, Pseudodog phantoms) are not scaled.

parameters.rationale:
How tough Bloodsuckers are — the invisible stalkers of the Zone. Includes the Mist, Ashy and prologue variants. Vanilla HP: 500.

Higher values mean longer, scarier close-range fights; every other mutant has its own card.
parameters.interaction: Changes only this mutant family's health. Other combat settings remain independent.

parameters.label: Bayun Attack Rate
parameters.description: How often a Bayun can use its attacks: claw swipes, leaps, pounces and dodges. Rate r writes cooldown multiplier 1/r for each of these cooldowns of every Bayun variant on the selected difficulty.

notes: Native per-agent, per-tag cooldown multiplier list of the selected difficulty (vanilla: Master only, 0.5).
Base cooldowns are AbilityPrototypes TriggeredCooldowns (seconds); agent entries match exact prototype SIDs, so every variant of the family is listed.
Families and tags the game never lists on Master need an in-game check.

parameters.rationale: How often Bayuns use their attacks — claw swipes, leaps, pounces and dodges (collar and quest variants included). Vanilla: 1× on Novice, Stalker and Veteran; 2× on Master (the game halves these cooldowns there). 2× = twice as often; 0.5× = twice the wait. The card shows the wait for one of them (claw every 5 s at 1×).
parameters.logic: Each attack has its own wait (cooldown) before it can be used again; this scales the waits of all the family's attacks. 1× keeps the game's timing. Its abilities (growls and blink teleports) are ABILITIES.
parameters.interaction: SPECIAL ABILITY RATE separately limits how often any mutant in the fight may use a special or knockdown move. How hard hits land is MUTANT HIT DAMAGE.

parameters.interaction: Each mutant's own ATTACK RATE still decides how soon that mutant can repeat its attacks.

parameters.label: Phantom Spawn Interval
parameters.description: Controls how long Psy encounters using the Master override wait before another phantom spawn cycle can begin.

notes: Novice/Stalker/Veteran contain no PsyPhantomNPCOverrides block; the UI represents absence as neutral 1.0 / Off. Creating equivalent overrides in Novice/Stalker/Veteran requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale:
In the Psy encounters that Master makes harder, how long you get before the next wave of phantoms appears. Lower = less breathing room.

Vanilla: 100% everywhere except Master, which halves the wait (50%).
parameters.logic: Lower percentages mean new phantom waves can return sooner. Master uses 50% of the normal wait time; 100% represents no extra Master override.
parameters.interaction: Pair this with Psy Phantom Count: shorter waits plus more phantoms can make an encounter far more intense.

parameters.label: Psy Phantom Count

parameters.rationale:
In those Master Psy encounters, how many phantoms come at you per wave. 200% doubles them.

Vanilla: 100% everywhere except Master (200%). Combine with a short spawn interval for a real nightmare.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps the normal count. 200% matches vanilla Master and doubles the configured phantom count.
parameters.interaction: Phantom Spawn Interval changes how quickly another wave can happen; this setting changes the size of each wave.

parameters.label: Sleep Threshold
parameters.description: Controls how tired the player must be before normal sleeping is allowed.

parameters.interaction: Separate no-sleep effects from hunger, bleeding, radiation or Psy can still block sleep regardless of this threshold.

parameters.description: Sets the minimum sleep duration used by the default sleep settings.
parameters.rationale: The shortest sleep you can pick. Vanilla: 7 hours. It doesn't change how much sleep heals you.

parameters.label: Radiation Accumulation
parameters.description: Scales the rate at which radiation is accumulated through the difficulty preset.
parameters.rationale:
How fast radiation builds up while you stand in contaminated areas. Higher = hotspots become deadly quickly.

Vanilla: Novice 0.6×, Stalker 1×, Veteran 1.5×, Master 1.85×.
parameters.interaction: Radiation Recovery controls passive reduction separately. Master Radiation Mechanics can also add a stamina penalty at high radiation.

parameters.label: Radiation Recovery
parameters.description: Controls how quickly accumulated radiation decreases naturally, in points per second.
parameters.rationale: How fast radiation drains away on its own without anti-rad or vodka. Vanilla: 0.05 points per second — slow, so meds still matter.
parameters.interaction: This acts on recovery, not exposure strength. Radiation Accumulation determines how quickly new radiation is gained.

parameters.label: Radiation Damage
parameters.description: Changes how much health damage accumulated radiation causes once radiation begins hurting you, without moving the vanilla radiation-state thresholds.

notes: Aggregate transform over the 11 runtime radiation-damage effect prototypes; radiation thresholds remain vanilla.
The runtime values are not replaced by one universal damage number; each stage keeps its original relative value.

parameters.rationale: How much health radiation eats once it becomes dangerous. 1× is vanilla, 2× doubles the damage; the warning levels stay where they are.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps vanilla radiation damage. 50% halves it, 200% doubles it, 600% multiplies it by six, and 1000% multiplies it by ten. Original stage thresholds stay vanilla.
parameters.interaction: Exposure determines how fast radiation builds up; recovery and Anti-Rad remove it. This setting only changes HP loss once radiation hurts.

parameters.label: Bleeding Severity
parameters.description: Scales the difficulty-wide bleeding effect applied by sources that cause bleeding.
parameters.rationale:
How bad bleeding wounds are overall. Higher = you bleed out faster and need bandages sooner.

Vanilla: Novice 0.25×, Stalker and Veteran 1×, Master 1.5×.
parameters.logic: Higher values make bleeding effects stronger overall; lower values soften them. Novice uses 25%, Stalker/Veteran 100%, and Master 150%.
parameters.interaction: Low / Medium / Severe Bleeding Damage decide how much HP you lose once each bleeding state is active. Natural Bleeding Recovery and medical treatment decide how quickly bleeding goes away.

parameters.label: Natural Bleeding Recovery
parameters.description: Controls the player's base natural bleeding reduction rate.
parameters.rationale: How fast bleeding stops on its own without bandages. Vanilla: 0.3. Raise it to shrug off scratches; lower it to make every wound need treatment.
parameters.interaction: Bandages and medkits apply direct bleeding removal independently of this passive rate.

parameters.label: Max Health
parameters.description: Changes your maximum health. The game's full-health feedback stays in sync with the new maximum.

notes: Direct MaxHP field is confirmed; broader assumptions about the 100-point HP scale require runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Your total health pool. Vanilla: 100 HP on every difficulty. More HP lets you survive more hits; healing items still restore the same flat amount, so each medkit covers a smaller share of a bigger pool.
parameters.interaction: The game keeps its vanilla low-health state boundary. Other systems may also assume a 100-point health scale, so very large Max Health changes should be tested in game.

parameters.label: Passive HP Regen
parameters.description: Controls ordinary passive health recovery on the player. Vanilla sets this to zero, so by default you do not slowly heal just by standing around.

notes: Field and vanilla value are confirmed; exact tick semantics and interaction with effect-based regeneration require runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: Slow healing over time without using anything. Vanilla: 0 — in the original game you never heal just by waiting. Even a small value makes minor wounds close up on their own.
parameters.logic: Zero keeps vanilla behavior. Raising it adds passive healing over time.
parameters.interaction: Health Recovery Delay decides when recovery can begin. Other healing sources, such as low-health recovery and medkits, stay separate.

parameters.label: Regen Delay
parameters.description: Vanilla player VitalParams define RegenHPDelayTimeSeconds = 5.

notes: The field explicitly uses seconds; the exact set of regeneration sources that honor it requires runtime validation.

parameters.rationale: How long after taking damage your health starts coming back. Vanilla: 5 seconds. Only matters if something is actually healing you, so with Passive HP Regen at 0 you may not notice it.
parameters.logic: Higher values postpone actor-level HP regeneration for longer; lower values shorten the configured delay.
parameters.interaction: If Passive HP Regen is set to 0, this delay may have no visible effect until another compatible health-recovery effect is active.

parameters.label: Health Regen Strength
parameters.description: Scales health regeneration produced by compatible recovery effects. It does not create passive healing by itself: 100% keeps full effect strength, while lower values weaken that recovery.
parameters.rationale: How strong all health recovery over time is. Vanilla: 100% on Novice and Stalker, 75% on Veteran, 50% on Master. Doesn't start healing by itself — it boosts or weakens healing that is already running.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps compatible regeneration effects at full strength. Lower values weaken them; higher values strengthen them. Vanilla uses 100% on Novice/Stalker, 75% on Veteran and 50% on Master.
parameters.interaction: Passive HP Regen is 0 in vanilla, so this matters mainly when another effect is already restoring health, such as low-health recovery.

parameters.label: Low-HP Recovery Rate
parameters.description: Controls the positive health-regeneration rate supplied by the normal low-health recovery effect. Vanilla uses 1.0; higher values recover health faster while the effect is active, and 0 disables this recovery contribution.
parameters.rationale: The small comeback heal the game gives you when you're almost dead. Vanilla: 100%. 0 removes it, so near-death means near-death; Master penalties can cut it further.
parameters.interaction: Health Regen Strength can scale this effect, and the Master low-health penalty can reduce it further.

parameters.label: Master Low-HP Penalties
parameters.description: Turns on the extra low-health punishment used by vanilla Master.
parameters.rationale: Master's extra punishment for being badly hurt: your health barely recovers until you patch up. Vanilla: OFF on Novice, Stalker and Veteran, ON on Master. The normal low-health system works either way.
parameters.logic: OFF leaves only the normal low-health system. ON adds the extra Master recovery penalty whenever the game enters its Master low-health state.
parameters.interaction: The game keeps the vanilla activation point for this state. The child control only changes how strong the recovery penalty is.

parameters.label: Master Low-HP Regen Loss
parameters.description: Controls how strongly Master difficulty slows health recovery when you are badly wounded.
parameters.rationale: How much that Master low-health punishment slows your healing. Vanilla: 70%. 0 removes it. Only works while Master Low-HP Penalties is ON.
parameters.logic: Higher values suppress health regeneration more strongly; zero removes this penalty component.
parameters.interaction: This remains inactive while Master Low-HP Penalties is OFF. It layers on top of ordinary low-health recovery and the Health Regen Strength setting.

parameters.label: Healing Amount
parameters.description: Changes how much HP the main healing items restore.
parameters.rationale: How much health one bandage gives back. Vanilla: 20 HP — a patch-up, not a full heal. Its bleed-stopping power is a separate setting.

parameters.label: Bandage Heal Time
parameters.description: Time in seconds over which this item restores HP.

notes: Original STALKER 2.1 GameData/EffectPrototypes.cfg: BandageHealing2 has Duration = 1.0 and Charges = 4 (DLC1 does not redefine it).
Only Duration is edited; total HP (ValueMin/ValueMax), bleeding, radiation and food effects stay independent.
In-game pacing of the 4 charges over a longer Duration still needs a runtime test.

parameters.rationale: How long the bandage's HP restore takes. Vanilla: 1 s — almost instant. Longer spreads the same 20 HP over more seconds, so you can't top up mid-fight.
parameters.logic: Sets Duration of BandageHealing2; the effect keeps its 4 charges and its total HP. 1 s = vanilla, 10 s = the same heal over ten seconds.
parameters.interaction: Drag this item's TIME column; right-click resets only this duration.

parameters.description: Time in seconds over which this item restores HP.

notes: Original STALKER 2.1 GameData/EffectPrototypes.cfg: MedkitHealing3 has Duration = 1.0 and Charges = 4 (DLC1 does not redefine it).
Only Duration is edited; total HP (ValueMin/ValueMax), bleeding, radiation and food effects stay independent.
In-game pacing of the 4 charges over a longer Duration still needs a runtime test.

parameters.rationale: How long the medkit's HP restore takes. Vanilla: 1 s — almost instant. Longer spreads the same 70 HP over more seconds, so you can't top up mid-fight.
parameters.logic: Sets Duration of MedkitHealing3; the effect keeps its 4 charges and its total HP. 1 s = vanilla, 10 s = the same heal over ten seconds.
parameters.interaction: Drag this item's TIME column; right-click resets only this duration.

parameters.description: Time in seconds over which this item restores HP.

notes: Original STALKER 2.1 GameData/EffectPrototypes.cfg: ArmyMedkitHealing4 has Duration = 1.0 and Charges = 4 (DLC1 does not redefine it).
Only Duration is edited; total HP (ValueMin/ValueMax), bleeding, radiation and food effects stay independent.
In-game pacing of the 4 charges over a longer Duration still needs a runtime test.

parameters.rationale: How long the army medkit's HP restore takes. Vanilla: 1 s — almost instant. Longer spreads the same 85 HP over more seconds, so you can't top up mid-fight.
parameters.logic: Sets Duration of ArmyMedkitHealing4; the effect keeps its 4 charges and its total HP. 1 s = vanilla, 10 s = the same heal over ten seconds.
parameters.interaction: Drag this item's TIME column; right-click resets only this duration.

parameters.label: Scientific Medkit Heal Time
parameters.description: Time in seconds over which this item restores HP.

notes: Original STALKER 2.1 GameData/EffectPrototypes.cfg: EcoMedkitHealing4 has Duration = 1.0 and Charges = 4 (DLC1 does not redefine it).
Only Duration is edited; total HP (ValueMin/ValueMax), bleeding, radiation and food effects stay independent.
In-game pacing of the 4 charges over a longer Duration still needs a runtime test.

parameters.rationale: How long the scientific medkit's HP restore takes. Vanilla: 1 s — almost instant. Longer spreads the same 100 HP over more seconds, so you can't top up mid-fight.
parameters.logic: Sets Duration of EcoMedkitHealing4; the effect keeps its 4 charges and its total HP. 1 s = vanilla, 10 s = the same heal over ten seconds.
parameters.interaction: Drag this item's TIME column; right-click resets only this duration.

parameters.label: Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much health a standard Medkit restores before any Master-only healing penalty is applied.
parameters.rationale: How much health a regular medkit gives back. Vanilla: 70 HP — most of a vanilla health bar.
parameters.interaction: Bleeding treatment is separate. If Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON, the Master Medkit Healing setting further changes the final heal.

parameters.label: Army Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much health an Army Medkit restores before any Master-only healing penalty is applied.
parameters.rationale: How much health an army medkit gives back. Vanilla: 85 HP.
parameters.interaction: Bleeding treatment is separate. If Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON, Master Army Medkit Healing further changes the final heal.

parameters.label: Scientific Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much health a Scientific Medkit restores. Vanilla restores 100 HP.
parameters.rationale: How much health a scientific medkit gives back. Vanilla: 100 HP — a full vanilla bar in one go.
parameters.interaction: Scientific Medkit bleeding and radiation treatment are separate. Vanilla Master does not apply the same healing penalty to Scientific Medkits that it applies to Bandages and the other Medkits.

parameters.label: Food Restores Health
parameters.description: Controls whether ordinary food restores health. This affects Bread, Fresh Bread, Canned Food, and Sausage only. Satiety and Weird Kettle alternative effects are intentionally unchanged.
parameters.rationale: Whether bread, fresh bread, canned food and sausage also heal you a bit. Vanilla: ON. Turn it OFF to make food only fix hunger, so medical items are your only way to heal.
parameters.logic: ON keeps vanilla food healing. OFF removes healing from the supported food items.
parameters.interaction: Bandage healing remains controlled by the Healing Amount radar. Weird Kettle alternative food effects are deliberately outside this switch.

parameters.label: Master Bandage Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much of the normal Bandage healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 25% of the normal heal.
parameters.rationale: How much of a bandage's heal you keep under Master's weaker meds. Vanilla: 25% — about 5 HP from a 20 HP bandage. 100% = no cut.
parameters.logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Bandage heal less. With the untouched base heal of 20 HP, vanilla Master gives about 5.0 HP.
parameters.interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

parameters.label: Master Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much of the normal Medkit healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 71% of the normal heal.
parameters.rationale: How much of a medkit's heal you keep under Master's weaker meds. Vanilla: 71% — about 50 HP from a 70 HP medkit. 100% = no cut.
parameters.logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Medkit heal less. With the untouched base heal of 70 HP, vanilla Master gives about 49.7 HP.
parameters.interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

parameters.label: Master Army Medkit Healing
parameters.description: Controls how much of the normal Army Medkit healing remains while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are active. Vanilla Master keeps 82% of the normal heal.
parameters.rationale: How much of an army medkit's heal you keep under Master's weaker meds. Vanilla: 82% — about 70 HP from an 85 HP army medkit. 100% = no cut.
parameters.logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Army Medkit heal less. With the untouched base heal of 85 HP, vanilla Master gives about 69.7 HP.
parameters.interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

parameters.label: Bandage Bleed Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much bleeding the Bandage removes when used.
parameters.rationale: How much bleeding one bandage stops. Vanilla: 100 — it fully stops any bleed. Lower it and a bad wound needs more than one bandage.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

parameters.label: Medkit Bleed Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much bleeding the Medkit removes when used.
parameters.rationale: How much bleeding a regular medkit stops. Vanilla: 15 — barely a dent, so you still want a bandage for a real bleed.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

parameters.label: Army Medkit Bleed Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much bleeding the Army Medkit removes when used.
parameters.rationale: How much bleeding an army medkit stops. Vanilla: 35.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

parameters.label: Scientific Medkit Bleed Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much bleeding the Scientific Medkit removes when used.
parameters.rationale: How much bleeding a scientific medkit stops. Vanilla: 25.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

parameters.label: Scientific Medkit Radiation Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much radiation the Scientific Medkit removes when used.
parameters.rationale: How much radiation a scientific medkit clears on top of healing. Vanilla: 60 — handy after a trip through a hot zone.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Radiation build-up and natural radiation recovery remain separate.

parameters.label: Anti-Rad Radiation Removal
parameters.description: Controls how much radiation the Anti-Rad removes when used.
parameters.rationale: How much radiation one anti-rad clears. Vanilla: 100 — a full cleanse. Lower it and heavy doses need more than one shot.
parameters.interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Radiation build-up and natural radiation recovery remain separate.

parameters.label: Max Stamina
parameters.description: Vanilla maximum stamina is 100. This changes the size of your stamina pool, not how fast it recovers or how much actions cost.
parameters.rationale: The size of your stamina bar. Vanilla: 100. A bigger bar lets you sprint, jump and swing longer before you're winded; recovery speed and action costs don't change.
parameters.interaction: Action costs are direct stamina values, so changing Maximum Stamina changes how many actions fit into a full bar even when their individual costs are untouched.

notes: Runtime 2.0.5 Player.VitalParams.MaxSP = 100.

parameters.label: Sprint Stops Below
parameters.description: Below this stamina value, sprinting is disabled. Default: 16.1 of the vanilla 100 stamina pool.
parameters.rationale: When your stamina drops below this, you can't sprint any more until it recovers. Vanilla: 16.1 out of 100. Lower it to squeeze out a longer final dash.
parameters.logic: Higher values make sprint lock out earlier while stamina is still relatively high; lower values let the player sprint deeper into the stamina bar.
parameters.interaction: Pairs with Exhaustion Regen Delay; sets sprint lockout, not sprint speed or stamina drain.

notes: The mapped threshold is the entry whose StateTags contains EStateTag::Sprint.

parameters.label: Exhaustion Regen Delay
parameters.description: Seconds before stamina regeneration resumes after sprint exhaustion.
parameters.rationale: How long you stand there gasping after sprinting yourself out before stamina starts coming back. Vanilla: 1 second.
parameters.logic: Higher values make exhaustion pauses last longer before recovery can resume; lower values shorten the pause.
parameters.interaction: Applies after sprint exhaustion; Sprint Stops Below determines the separate lockout threshold.

parameters.label: Boost Starts Below
parameters.description: Below this stamina value, the separate low-stamina recovery boost becomes eligible. Default: 30 stamina.
parameters.rationale: When stamina falls below this, the game gives you a short second-wind boost. Vanilla: 30 out of 100.
parameters.logic: Higher values allow the low-stamina recovery helper to engage across a larger portion of the bar; lower values reserve it for near-exhaustion.
parameters.interaction: Pairs with low-stamina Boost Rate and low-stamina Boost Duration, not the sprint lockout threshold.

notes: The NormalSP boundary is 30; the LowSPThreshold branch starts at 0 and applies IncreaseStaminaPoints below that boundary.

parameters.label: Boost Strength
parameters.description: Regeneration strength of the temporary low-stamina recovery boost (10 stamina/s originally).
parameters.rationale: How strong that second wind is. Vanilla: 10 stamina per second on top of normal recovery. 0 removes it.
parameters.logic: Higher values make the emergency recovery effect stronger; lower values make low-stamina recovery closer to the ordinary base rate.
parameters.interaction: Boost Starts Below sets its trigger; low-stamina Boost Duration sets how long it lasts.

parameters.label: Boost Duration
parameters.description: Seconds that the conditional low-stamina stamina regeneration boost remains active (4 seconds originally).
parameters.rationale: How long the second wind lasts once it kicks in. Vanilla: 4 seconds.
parameters.logic: Higher values keep the low-stamina recovery effect active longer; lower values shorten the boost.
parameters.interaction: Boost Activates Below sets the trigger; low-stamina Boost Rate sets the boost strength.

parameters.label: Speed-Limited Sprint Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery while you are sprinting but your movement speed is being limited. The game decides when this slower sprint state is active.
parameters.rationale: Stamina drain when you hold sprint but the game limits you to a slower speed. Vanilla: −0.65, the same as normal running. The game decides when this state applies.
parameters.logic: More negative values suppress recovery more strongly; zero adds no state penalty; positive values help recovery. Do not read this as a separate 'slow sprint' button.
parameters.interaction: This works alongside normal Sprint stamina behavior. Encumbrance and other movement limits can affect when the game uses this slower sprint state.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in speed-limited sprint state

notes: CFG target is confirmed; exact runtime transition into EStateTag::SprintUnderRunSpeed is not fully documented.

parameters.label: Jogging-State Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery during the game's lighter running movement state. There is no separate Jogging keybind.
parameters.rationale: Stamina effect while the game counts you as jogging. Vanilla: 0 — no drain. There's no jog key; the game picks this state itself.
parameters.logic: Negative settings slow stamina recovery while jogging; 0 is neutral; positive settings help stamina recover.
parameters.interaction: The game decides when your movement counts as jogging. This setting only affects stamina recovery during that movement.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal Jogging state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::Jogging is confirmed; there is no separate player Jogging bind and exact activation semantics require runtime verification.

parameters.label: Slow-Run-State Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery during the game's slow-running movement state. There is no separate Slow Run keybind.
parameters.rationale: Stamina effect while the game counts you as slow-running. Vanilla: 0 — no drain. There's no key for it; the game picks this state itself.
parameters.logic: Negative values add a stamina penalty in the SlowRun state; zero is neutral; positive values help recovery. Do not treat this as the game's Walk toggle.
parameters.interaction: This is separate from walking. The game decides when movement counts as slow running.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal SlowRun state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::SlowRun is confirmed; SlowRunThreshold = 0.5 exists, but its complete state-selection semantics are not proven.

parameters.label: Vault Height
parameters.description: Changes the tallest obstacle you can vault over. The WAIST / EYES / ABOVE EYES markers are simple player-friendly height references.
parameters.rationale: The tallest obstacle you can climb over. Vanilla: 130 — the WAIST / EYES markers show what that means in-game. Raise it to vault fences and crates that used to block you.
parameters.logic: Higher lets you vault taller obstacles; lower restricts vaulting. This changes height reach, not jump distance.
parameters.interaction: Vault stamina cost, landing rules and collision checks remain independent.

notes: The CFG field and vanilla value are confirmed from runtime 2.0.5.
WAIST/EYES/ABOVE EYES are practical UI orientation points; exact reachable world geometry depends on the rest of VaultingParams and collision/animation constraints.

parameters.label: Medium-Water Stamina Drain
parameters.description: Changes the extra stamina drain while moving through medium-depth water.
parameters.rationale: Extra stamina lost while wading through waist-deep water. Vanilla: 1. 0 makes wading free.
parameters.logic: Higher percentages make movement actions consume more stamina while moderately immersed; lower values soften the water penalty.
parameters.interaction: This changes penalty strength only. Water immersion thresholds remain unchanged.

notes: AffectedStaminaActionTypes: Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Vault.

parameters.label: Deep-Water Stamina Drain
parameters.description: Changes the extra stamina drain while moving through deep water.
parameters.rationale: Extra stamina lost while pushing through deep water. Vanilla: 2 — deep water wears you out fast.
parameters.logic: Higher percentages make deep-water movement substantially more expensive; lower values reduce that stamina pressure.
parameters.interaction: This does not change the water-depth thresholds or the separate deadly-water instant-death effect.

notes: AffectedStaminaActionTypes: Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Vault.
Deadly water still has a separate WaterDeadlyDamage instant-death effect.

parameters.label: Stamina Regen
parameters.description: Controls the player's base stamina regeneration rate.
parameters.rationale: How fast your stamina refills when you ease off. Vanilla: 5 per second. Higher = shorter breathers between sprints.
parameters.interaction: Movement-state values, hunger penalties and fatigue effects can reduce this base regeneration in context.

parameters.label: Action Costs
parameters.description: Changes stamina pressure from common player actions.
parameters.rationale: How much stamina sprinting burns. Vanilla: 5.25. Lower it to run further; raise it to make every dash count. Jump, vault and melee costs have their own bars.

parameters.label: Jump Stamina Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a jump.
parameters.rationale: Stamina spent on every jump. Vanilla: 16 — about six jumps empty a full bar.
parameters.interaction: This is a per-action cost and does not change stamina regeneration.

parameters.label: Vault Stamina Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by vaulting.
parameters.rationale: Stamina spent on every vault over an obstacle. Vanilla: 12.
parameters.interaction: The effect is independent of jump cost even though both affect traversal.

parameters.label: Quick Melee Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a quick melee attack.
parameters.rationale: Stamina spent on each quick knife swing. Vanilla: 16.
parameters.interaction: Strong melee and buttstock attacks have independent costs.

parameters.label: Strong Melee Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a strong melee attack.
parameters.rationale: Stamina spent on each heavy knife swing. Vanilla: 25 — four in a row and you're out of breath.
parameters.interaction: This does not alter melee damage, only the stamina economy of the action.

parameters.label: Buttstock Melee Cost
parameters.description: Controls stamina consumed by a buttstock melee attack.
parameters.rationale: Stamina spent on each rifle-butt strike. Vanilla: 12.
parameters.interaction: Normal and strong melee use their own stamina values.

parameters.label: Full Sprint Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery while sprinting.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in full sprint state

notes: Player-facing Sprint action; CFG target EStateTag::Sprint is confirmed.

parameters.rationale: How hard full sprinting drains you. Vanilla: −1.4 (a strong drain). Closer to 0 = you can sprint much longer.
parameters.logic: Lower recovery makes sustained sprinting more exhausting. 0 adds no sprint-specific recovery change; higher recovery lets stamina come back faster.
parameters.interaction: Stacks with Base Stamina Regeneration and the separate Sprint Stamina Drain. Speed-limited sprinting can use the separate SprintUnderRunSpeed state instead.

parameters.label: Run-State Stamina Effect
parameters.description: Changes stamina recovery while the game treats your movement as running.

display.valueLabel: Stamina effect in internal Run state

notes: CFG target EStateTag::Run is confirmed; exact state-selection semantics versus Jogging/SlowRun require runtime verification.

parameters.rationale: How much normal running drains stamina. Vanilla: −0.65. Closer to 0 = running costs less.
parameters.logic: Negative settings slow stamina recovery while running; 0 is neutral; positive settings help stamina recover.
parameters.interaction: The game switches between several movement states depending on how you move. This setting affects only normal running.

parameters.label: Aiming Regen Penalty
parameters.description: Percent reduction in stamina regeneration specifically while aiming; 0% removes the penalty.

notes: Player-facing Aim state; CFG target EStateTag::Aim is confirmed.
UI stores a positive penalty magnitude; production writer emits the corresponding negative CFG coefficient via negateSet.

parameters.rationale: How much slower stamina refills while you aim down sights. Vanilla: −25%. 0 lets you catch your breath at full speed while aiming.
parameters.logic: Higher settings slow stamina recovery more while aiming. 0 removes the aiming recovery penalty.
parameters.interaction: This is a continuous recovery-state penalty, not a one-time stamina charge. Base Stamina Recovery sets the underlying recovery rate; Sprint, Jump, Vault and melee costs remain independent.

parameters.label: Maximum Carry Weight
parameters.description: Sets the player's default maximum inventory mass.
parameters.rationale: How much you can carry before you get slowed down. Vanilla: 80 kg. Raise it to haul more loot; lower it for a tighter backpack.
parameters.interaction: Encumbrance thresholds and equipment-derived carry-weight bonuses can affect how the load feels before the absolute maximum is reached.

parameters.label: Corpse Supply Reduction
parameters.description: Reduces optional Food, Drinks and Medical source Chance on the 92 ordinary-human loadout generators (roaming GeneralNPC_* and settlement GuardNPC_*), plus native bonus Corpse SmartLoot group spawn endpoints. This is not a percentage of corpses that will be empty.

targets.path: 104 private-cloned item Chance rows + selected CorpseSmartLoot native group spawn endpoints

notes: Source Chance is scaled last after the per-item Chance overrides and Standard Med multiplier.
All optional bonus packages use their original 39 rank/caliber/consumable group spawn endpoints, not Weapon Attached Ammo or the normal NPC equipment generator.
0% is a no-op; 100% keeps ordinary NPC gear intact and removes the optional CorpseSmartLoot package on the selected difficulty.
Engine execution of new spawn endpoints requires fresh-NPC validation.

parameters.rationale: Makes ordinary human bodies carry less food, drinks and meds. Vanilla: 0 — no change. Higher = leaner pickings, so you rely more on stashes and traders. Weapons, their loaded ammo, armor and quest/special NPCs are never touched.
parameters.logic: Chance rows and optional Corpse SmartLoot group activation are reduced separately. 0% leaves their original behavior; 100% disables eligible ordinary supplies.
parameters.interaction: Does not change the saved SmartLoot package choice, Bonus Ammo Qty, Mod Items or the individually configured raw Chance values.

parameters.label: NPC Smart Loot
parameters.description: Enable or disable optional Medicine, Ammo and Water corpse SmartLoot packages, preserving their saved selections.

notes: ON keeps the selected optional corpse SmartLoot packages.
OFF writes an empty CorpseSmartLoot subtree for the selected difficulty while preserving all package selections and bonus settings in presets.
Normal NPC consumables, ordinary gear and the independent stash SmartLoot switch are unaffected.

parameters.rationale: Turn optional corpse Smart Loot packs on or off. Turning it off removes bonus Medicine, Ammo and Water packages from ordinary NPC corpses without changing their regular loot.
parameters.logic: OFF clears the native CorpseSmartLoot entry; ON uses the saved package selection.
parameters.interaction: The three package chips, NEED BOOST and bonus ammo controls stay saved but are inactive when OFF.

parameters.label: Corpse Smart Loot
parameters.description: Toggles the three authored extra corpse SmartLoot packages (Medicine, Ammo, Water) independently; any combination, including none, is a valid native list. Standard NPC consumables and carried weapon loot remain independent.
parameters.rationale: Extra loot packages ordinary human bodies can carry: Medicine, Ammo and Water, in any combination. Vanilla: Novice gets Medicine + Ammo, Stalker gets Water, Veteran and Master get none.
parameters.logic: Each chip adds one native SmartLoot package to EconomyDifficulty.CorpseSmartLoot.GeneralNPC of the selected difficulty, written in the canonical order Medicine, Ammo, Water. Vanilla authors Medicine + Ammo (Novice), Water (Stalker) and none (Veteran, Master); other combinations are the same list format.
parameters.interaction: Bonus ammo quantity applies whenever the Ammo package is on. Standard medical items are not switched off by any package choice.

parameters.label: Standard NPC Medical
parameters.description: Changes standard human consumable-generator medical Chance relative to each native CFG entry. This is independent of the optional corpse SmartLoot medicine package and does not modify stack quantities.

targets.path: medical PossibleItems[*].Chance via standard-human-only redirect manifest

notes: The audited control surface contains 58 medical Chance rows across six shared role-oriented consumable pools.
100% preserves every vanilla Chance; 0% disables those medical rolls; values above 100% multiply each source Chance and clamp at 100%.
Seven source medical rows are already Chance = 1.0 and therefore remain capped at 100% when increasing frequency.

92 ordinary-human SubItemGenerator links (88 base + 4 DLC1 NORD; roaming GeneralNPC_* and settlement GuardNPC_*) are redirected to TCD-owned pool clones; disabled Prologue edges, named MIK, unspawned No_Armor roots, zombies (which re-declare their own link) and the shared vanilla pools themselves remain vanilla.

parameters.rationale: How often ordinary human enemies carry their usual meds. Vanilla: 1× (the game's own chances). 0 = they never carry meds; 2× = twice as likely.
parameters.logic: A relative 0–200% scaler of each native consumable-generator medical Chance.
parameters.interaction: Always editable, including when Corpse Smart Loot is Water or None; does not affect zombies, quests, traders or stashes.

parameters.label: Bonus Ammo Amount
parameters.description: Changes MinCount/MaxCount in additional NPC_Ammo_Smart corpse ammo stacks, only when the Ammo SmartLoot package is on. This is ammo quantity, not item drop Chance, loaded-magazine ammo or breakable-box loot.

notes: Exact source data: 43 NPC_Ammo_Smart item rows across 24 PrimaryWeaponParams groups and four ranks; matches GameData/StashPrototypes.cfg supplied dump row-for-row (FNV32 0x61073f67).

Only MinCount/MaxCount are scaled in a source-derived clone with integer-half-up rounding; native MinSpawnChance, MaxSpawnChance, PriorityCaliber, MainWeaponAmmoCount, Weight and item/rank eligibility remain inherited.
Only the selected difficulty GeneralNPC CorpseSmartLoot list references the clone. The Ammo package activates it; without it the player-selected multiplier saved but causes no ammo override.
Breakable ammo uses the separate ItemGeneratorPrototypes.cfg DestructibleStash_AmmoSNG/NATO generator clones and is never affected by this control.
Legacy weapon-attached AmmoMinCount/AmmoMaxCount edits on 121 NPC weapon rows are retired (242 direct edit points removed).
Actual in-game corpse drop result and source-derived clone inheritance require a Wine build and runtime test.

parameters.rationale: How many rounds the bonus Ammo package gives when it drops. Vanilla: 1×. Only matters while the Ammo package is on; the ammo loaded in their guns stays the same.
parameters.logic: The 0–3× amount multiplier scales only original MinCount/MaxCount. Zero removes these optional stacks; progression rank still controls which calibers can appear.
parameters.interaction: Active only when the Ammo package of Corpse Smart Loot is on; otherwise this value stays saved but inactive.

parameters.label: NPC Weapon Condition
parameters.description: Sets the actual minimum and maximum condition of weapons carried by ordinary repeatable human NPC loadouts. Vanilla is left untouched until this control is changed.

notes: Production-only audit locks this control to 738 direct weapon rows (WeaponPrimary/Secondary/Pistol) across 92 ordinary-human loadout roots: roaming GeneralNPC_* and settlement GuardNPC_*, including 40 DLC1 NORD rows.

736 rows use vanilla 25%-50% durability ranges; two authored outliers use 35%-45% (Corpus guard) and 45%-45% (Freedom guard). OFF/default behavior emits no patch, so those outliers remain untouched. Grenade (Artifact enum) and armor durability rows are never edited.
Once either bound is changed, the selected MIN and MAX become direct MinDurability/MaxDurability values on all 738 audited weapon rows.
Two Prologue roots, four named MIK/Mykluha roots and three spawner-less No_Armor roots are excluded.

parameters.rationale: How worn the guns you pick up from ordinary human enemies are. Untouched = the game's own condition rolls. Push it down to make looted guns repair projects; up to make them worth keeping.
parameters.logic: Higher MIN improves the worst condition you can find. Higher MAX allows better-condition weapons; MIN cannot exceed MAX.
parameters.interaction: Changes only the condition of weapons dropped by ordinary human enemies. It does not change which weapons they use, their ammo, health, traders, zombies, or story characters.

parameters.label: Stash Supply Reduction
parameters.description: Keeps (100% − X) of the game's supply odds in ordinary Basic (including the six DLC1 CheapNoFresh stashes), Standard and Rare stashes and in smart world stashes: Chance rows roll less often, Weight lists get an appended native Empty pick with the removed share, and smart world groups get lower spawn chances. Stack sizes stay vanilla. Quest, unique and protected stashes are never touched.

targets.path: guarded 41 tier groups and 422 source World SmartLoot group endpoints

notes: Weight lists use the native Empty pick (runtime test: RELEASE-TESTING.md, Stash presence).
Until 2026-11-16 Weight lists only lost stack size, so one-item Basic food/drink/bandage/coupon picks did not change below 100%.

parameters.rationale: Makes ordinary stashes come up empty more often. Vanilla: 0% — no change. 50% = every supply item turns up half as often (food, meds, drinks, ammo, coupons alike); the amount you get when it does stays the same. Quest and special stashes are never touched.
parameters.logic: 0% keeps the game's odds; 50% halves the odds of every supply item; 100% leaves these stashes without optional supplies. Same rule for every list type.

parameters.label: Mutant Parts Cost

parameters.label: Guide Travel Fees

parameters.logic: 100% keeps vanilla guide prices. 50% halves paid routes, 200% doubles them, and 0% makes paid routes free.
parameters.interaction: Roaming-guide base fees and minimum price scale with this slider on STALKER 2.1+. Native difficulty, reputation, region and rounding rules still apply.

parameters.label: Upgrade Cost
parameters.description: Upgrade_Cost is a direct difficulty setting: 100% on Novice/Stalker, 125% on Veteran and 150% on Master.
parameters.rationale: Price of weapon and armor upgrades. Vanilla: 100% on Novice and Stalker, 125% on Veteran, 150% on Master. Which upgrades exist doesn't change.
parameters.interaction: Each upgrade still has its own base price. This setting makes upgrades generally cheaper or more expensive without changing their relative costs.

parameters.label: Base Repair Cost
parameters.description: Sets the overall baseline for repair prices. Vanilla is 70%. Use it to make repairs cheaper or more expensive everywhere.

parameters.label: Disliked Repair Price

parameters.interaction: Base Repair Cost and the faction's current attitude both affect the final price.

parameters.label: Neutral Repair Price
parameters.description: Changes repair prices when your reputation with the technician's faction is Neutral. Vanilla is 1x of the base repair price.

parameters.interaction: Base Repair Cost and the faction's current attitude both affect the final price.

parameters.label: Friendly Repair Price
parameters.description: Changes repair prices when your reputation with the technician's faction is Friend. Vanilla is 0.75x of the base repair price.
parameters.rationale: Repair price when the technician's faction likes you. Vanilla: 0.75× — a friend's discount.
parameters.logic: Higher means more expensive repairs from friendly technicians; lower means cheaper repairs at this reputation level.
parameters.interaction: Base Repair Cost and the faction's current attitude both affect the final price.

parameters.rationale: Coupons you get for side quests. Vanilla: 135% on Novice, 100% on Stalker, 75% on Veteran, 55% on Master.
parameters.interaction: Main Quest Coupons are adjusted independently. This does not change stash rewards or starting money.

parameters.label: Armor Durability
parameters.description: Changes how quickly armor loses condition. Higher settings make armor last longer; lower settings make it wear out faster.
parameters.rationale: How long your armor holds up before it's falling apart. Vanilla: 1.35× on Novice, 1× on Stalker, 0.9× on Veteran, 0.6× on Master. Higher = fewer repair trips; protection itself doesn't change.
parameters.interaction: Changes armor condition durability only. It does not change armor protection values, weapon wear or jamming thresholds.

parameters.label: Ammo Weight

parameters.interaction: Carry-capacity and encumbrance controls remain separate. This changes item Weight itself, so existing inventory-weight rules continue to apply normally.

parameters.label: Consumable Weight

parameters.rationale: How heavy food and meds are in your backpack. Vanilla: 1×. 0× = weightless. Their effects don't change.
parameters.interaction: This does not change consumable effect strength or duration. DLC1 dry-ration weight is patched only when DLC1 is installed.

parameters.rationale: How heavy weapons are in your backpack. Vanilla: 1×. Lower it to carry a spare rifle without being slowed down; damage and handling don't change.

parameters.label: Global Anomaly Damage
parameters.description: This is the broad anomaly difficulty setting. It scales damaging anomaly output as a group while each anomaly keeps its own base damage value.
parameters.rationale: How much all damaging anomalies hurt, on top of each anomaly's own damage. Vanilla: 0.3× on Novice, 1× on Stalker, 1.45× on Veteran, 1.75× on Master. Your suit's protection still applies after this.
parameters.logic: Higher raises the global damage multiplier; lower reduces it. Individual anomaly damage settings still apply.
parameters.interaction: Individual anomaly damage and this global setting combine before armor and other protection.

parameters.label: Master Starvation Penalties
parameters.description: Enables the extra starvation punishment bundle that vanilla Master adds on top of the normal hunger system. It is a discrete mechanics switch, not another hunger setting.
parameters.rationale: Master's starvation punishment once you're severely hungry: actions cost much more stamina, you lose health every few seconds and stop healing. Vanilla: OFF on Novice, Stalker and Veteran, ON on Master. Normal hunger effects work either way.
parameters.logic: When the game reaches its severe-hunger state, this bundle adds +200% stamina drain, periodic 4 HP starvation damage on a 10-second interval after its delay, and -100% health regeneration. OFF leaves only the normal hunger effects.
parameters.interaction: The game keeps the vanilla starvation activation point. The child controls only change stamina drain, damage, interval, delay and health-recovery strength.

parameters.label: Radiation Stamina Penalty
parameters.description: Enables the additional Master radiation penalty rather than changing radiation accumulation or radiation damage itself.
parameters.rationale: Master's extra stamina cost while you're heavily irradiated. Vanilla: OFF on Novice, Stalker and Veteran, ON on Master. Radiation still builds up and hurts you either way.
parameters.logic: When the game enters the heavy-radiation state used by this Master bundle, it adds an extra stamina-drain penalty (50% in vanilla). The normal radiation system remains active either way.
parameters.interaction: The activation point stays vanilla. Radiation Accumulation and Radiation Recovery determine how quickly the player reaches and leaves that state.

parameters.label: Master Severe-Fatigue Penalties
parameters.description: Enables the Master-only severe-fatigue penalty bundle. This is separate from ordinary sleepiness build-up, aiming-time penalties and reload penalties.
parameters.rationale: Master's punishment for being exhausted: smaller stamina bar, less carry capacity, more recoil, more sway and wider spread. Vanilla: OFF on Novice, Stalker and Veteran, ON on Master. Normal tiredness effects work either way.
parameters.logic: When the game enters the Master severe-fatigue state, this bundle adds -20% maximum stamina, -20% carry capacity, +55% recoil, extra aim sway and shot spread in vanilla.
parameters.interaction: The activation point stays vanilla. The child controls only change how strong each severe-fatigue penalty becomes.

parameters.label: Well-Fed Stamina Recovery Bonus
parameters.description: Changes the stamina-recovery bonus you get while well fed. Vanilla gives +20%.
parameters.rationale: Bonus stamina recovery while your stomach is full. Vanilla: +20% — a reward for eating before a fight. 0 removes it.
parameters.logic: Higher values reward staying well fed with stronger stamina recovery; zero removes the bonus. The supported UI range does not turn this lowest-hunger state into a penalty.
parameters.interaction: The game keeps the vanilla boundary for leaving the well-fed state. Stamina Regen in the Stamina tab sets the underlying regeneration rate.

parameters.label: Starvation Action Cost
parameters.description: Changes the extra stamina cost of actions while the Master starvation penalty is active. Vanilla adds +200%.
parameters.rationale: How much more stamina actions cost while you're starving under Master rules. Vanilla: +200% — three times the normal cost. 0 removes the extra.
parameters.logic: 100% means +100% extra stamina cost, not normal cost. 0% removes this extra starvation cost.
parameters.interaction: Severe hunger also slows stamina recovery. This changes the extra cost of actions, not an ongoing drain.

parameters.label: Starvation Damage
parameters.description: The Master starvation bundle applies a dedicated Hunger damage effect with a vanilla value of 4 per charge.
parameters.rationale: Health lost each time starvation hits under Master rules. Vanilla: 4 HP. 0 = starving no longer hurts directly.
parameters.logic: Higher values increase each starvation-damage charge; zero retains the bundle but removes direct HP damage from this component.
parameters.interaction: Starvation Damage Interval controls how often the charge repeats, while Starvation Penalty Delay controls when this effect begins after activation.

parameters.label: Starvation Damage Interval
parameters.description: Vanilla schedules the starvation damage charge every 10 seconds while the effect remains active.
parameters.rationale: Seconds between starvation hits. Vanilla: 10. Lower = the same damage comes faster.
parameters.logic: Lower values make the same damage arrive more frequently; higher values spread the damage out over a longer interval.
parameters.interaction: Practical starvation pressure depends on both this interval and Starvation Damage.

parameters.label: Starvation Penalty Delay
parameters.description: All three vanilla starvation penalties use a 3-second delay. This control keeps those delay values synchronized.
parameters.rationale: Grace period before the starvation penalties kick in. Vanilla: 3 seconds.
parameters.logic: Lower values make the penalties engage sooner after the starvation state activates; higher values provide a longer grace period.
parameters.interaction: Master Starvation Penalties decides whether this bundle exists. This control only changes the grace period before its active penalties begin.

parameters.label: Starvation Health Recovery Penalty
parameters.description: Vanilla Master applies a 100% health-recovery penalty while the starvation bundle is active.
parameters.rationale: How much starving blocks your healing under Master rules. Vanilla: 100% — no healing at all. 0 removes it.
parameters.logic: Higher values suppress health regeneration more strongly; zero removes this component.
parameters.interaction: This acts on regeneration rather than direct damage, so it combines with Starvation Damage and the Health tab regeneration settings.

parameters.label: Light Fatigue Aim Delay
parameters.description: At the Low Sleepiness state, vanilla increases aiming time by 15%.
parameters.rationale: How much light tiredness slows your aiming. Vanilla: +15% time to aim.
parameters.logic: Higher values make aiming settle more slowly once the low-fatigue threshold is crossed; zero removes this standard low-fatigue aiming penalty.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla low-fatigue state.

parameters.label: Medium Fatigue Aim Delay
parameters.description: Vanilla raises the aiming-time penalty to +25% in the medium fatigue state.
parameters.rationale: How much moderate tiredness slows your aiming. Vanilla: +25% time to aim.
parameters.logic: Higher values further slow aiming during medium fatigue; zero removes this component.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla medium-fatigue state, replacing the low-state aiming penalty.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Aim Delay
parameters.description: Vanilla increases aiming time by +40% in the severe fatigue state.
parameters.rationale: How much severe tiredness slows your aiming. Vanilla: +40% time to aim — sleep before a big fight.
parameters.logic: Higher values make severe fatigue more disruptive to aiming; zero removes this standard aiming-time component.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla severe-fatigue state.

parameters.label: Medium Fatigue Reload Delay
parameters.description: Medium fatigue adds +15% to the reload-time effect in vanilla.
parameters.rationale: How much moderate tiredness slows your reloads. Vanilla: +15% reload time.
parameters.logic: Higher values lengthen reloads more while medium fatigue is active; zero removes this penalty.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla medium-fatigue state. It is separate from the aiming-time penalty.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Reload Delay
parameters.description: Controls how much severe fatigue slows your reloads. Vanilla severe fatigue adds 18.75% reload time.
parameters.rationale: How much severe tiredness slows your reloads. Vanilla: +18.75% reload time. Master fatigue can add more.
parameters.logic: Higher values make reloads slower while severely fatigued. Zero removes this reload penalty.
parameters.interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla severe-fatigue state. Master Severe-Fatigue Penalties can add another layer on top.

parameters.label: Sleep HP Restore
parameters.description: Controls how much HP normal sleep restores when you wake up. Starts at 300 HP; adjustable from 0 to 600 HP.
parameters.rationale: How much health a full night's sleep gives back. Vanilla: 300 HP. 0 makes sleep stop healing you; up to 600 HP turns a night in a safe bed into a full patch-up.
parameters.logic: The original effect restores 300 HP on waking. Set 0 HP to disable this recovery or up to 600 HP to increase it; reset returns to 300 HP.
parameters.interaction: Medkits and passive HP regeneration remain separate.

parameters.label: Sleep Stamina Restore
parameters.description: Normal sleep restores stamina with a vanilla +100% Stamina effect.
parameters.rationale: How much stamina you wake up with after sleeping. Vanilla: a full bar (+100%).
parameters.interaction: This affects the post-sleep restore, not passive stamina regeneration or action costs.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Stamina Loss
parameters.description: Vanilla Master reduces maximum stamina by 20% while its severe-fatigue bundle is active.
parameters.rationale: How much of your stamina bar you lose while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: 20%. 0 removes it.
parameters.logic: Higher values reduce the available stamina pool further; zero removes this component.
parameters.interaction: Max Stamina defines your normal pool; this loss applies only during Master severe fatigue.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Carry Loss
parameters.description: Vanilla Master applies a 20% loss to both the additional-inventory-weight and penalty-less-weight fatigue effects.
parameters.rationale: How much carry capacity you lose while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: 20%. 0 removes it.
parameters.logic: Higher values make fatigue reduce carrying capability more strongly; zero removes both carry-related components together.
parameters.interaction: Your normal carrying limit and equipment carry bonuses remain separate.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Recoil
parameters.description: Vanilla Master adds a +55% recoil effect while the severe-fatigue bundle is active.
parameters.rationale: How much harder your guns kick while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: +55% recoil. 0 removes it.
parameters.interaction: This stacks with other recoil sources but does not change reload or aim-time penalties.

parameters.label: Severe-Fatigue Aim Sway
parameters.description: Controls how much extra weapon sway Master severe fatigue adds while aiming.
parameters.rationale: How much more your sights wobble while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: +40%. 0 removes it.
parameters.interaction: Recoil and bullet spread are separate penalties in the same Master fatigue bundle.

parameters.label: Severe Fatigue Bullet Spread
parameters.description: Changes how much severe fatigue increases weapon spread.
parameters.rationale: How much wider your shots spread while exhausted under Master rules. Vanilla: +50%. 0 removes it.
parameters.interaction: Recoil and aim sway are separate penalties in the same Master fatigue bundle.

parameters.label: Master Radiation Stamina Cost Increase
parameters.description: When Master Radiation Mechanics is active at heavy radiation, this adds an extra stamina cost to stamina-consuming actions. Vanilla is +50%; 0% removes the extra stamina cost.

display.valueLabel: Extra stamina cost under heavy radiation

parameters.rationale: How much more stamina actions cost while heavily irradiated under Master rules. Vanilla: +50%. 0 removes it.
parameters.logic: 50% means +50% extra stamina cost. 0% removes this extra radiation cost.

parameters.rationale: Health lost per tick from a severe bleed. Vanilla: 2 HP — that adds up fast without a bandage.
parameters.interaction: Applies while the game is in its vanilla severe-bleeding state. Bleeding Effect Strength can further change how dangerous bleeding feels overall.

parameters.label: Flycatcher Movement Speed
parameters.description: Controls how much of your normal movement speed remains while the Flycatcher slowdown is active.

notes: Runtime CFG 2.0.5 stores FlycatcherVelocityChange as -50%. The UI exposes retained movement speed instead: CFG delta = UI value - 1.0.

parameters.rationale: How fast you can still move when a Flycatcher grabs you. Vanilla: 50% of normal speed. 100% = no slowdown; 0% = stuck in place.
parameters.logic: Vanilla applies a -50% velocity change, so 50% of normal movement speed remains. 100% means no movement slowdown; 0% corresponds to a -100% velocity change.
parameters.interaction: Changes only player movement slowdown inside the Flycatcher. Projectile slowdown, HP/stamina regeneration penalties and turn slowdown remain separate.

parameters.label: Flycatcher Turn Speed
parameters.description: Controls how much of your normal look/turn speed remains while the Flycatcher slowdown is active.

notes: Runtime CFG 2.0.5 stores both yaw and pitch effects as -0.7. One UI value intentionally drives both targets: CFG delta = UI value - 1.0.

parameters.rationale: How fast you can still turn and look around inside a Flycatcher. Vanilla: 30% of normal. 100% = no slowdown.
parameters.logic: Vanilla applies -0.7 to both yaw and pitch turn-rate effects, leaving 30% of normal turn speed. 100% means no turn slowdown; 0% corresponds to -1.0 on both effects.
parameters.interaction: The same setting is applied to Flycatcher yaw and pitch so horizontal and vertical looking stay synchronized. Movement speed is controlled separately.

parameters.label: Clicker Health Damage
parameters.description: Controls the direct health damage dealt by a Clicker hit without changing the anomaly's equipment corrosion or behavior.
parameters.rationale: How much health a Clicker hit takes. Vanilla: 70 base damage. Only the health damage changes; the hit still wears down your gear as usual.
parameters.logic: Vanilla ClickerAnomalyHit deals 70 base Burn damage before the normal anomaly-difficulty/protection layers are resolved. 100% keeps that base value; 0% removes this direct health-damage component.
parameters.interaction: This slider changes only the ClickerAnomalyHit base value. Global anomaly difficulty and player protection remain separate layers; Clicker equipment corrosion is intentionally untouched.

parameters.label: Glass Shards Health Damage
parameters.description: Scales Glass Shards health damage at both movement-speed tiers while preserving the stronger high-speed hit.

notes: Runtime CFG stores low-speed Glass Shards damage as 20-25 and high-speed damage as 100. The slider scales both tiers together and leaves MinSpeed/MaxSpeed thresholds unchanged.

parameters.rationale: How much health Glass Shards take as you move through them. Vanilla: 100%. Running through still hurts more than walking.
parameters.logic: 100% keeps vanilla Glass Shards damage. 0% removes its health damage; 200% doubles both low-speed and high-speed damage.
parameters.interaction: Glass Shards Bleeding and Glass Shards equipment corrosion remain separate effects. This control does not change the anomaly speed thresholds.

parameters.label: Glass Shards Bleeding
